speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To better understand your painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg, can you tell me how long you have had this symptom and if you recall any specific event, such as a trip or insect bite, that might have caused it?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given your history of Crohn's disease, diabetes, and recent corticosteroid use, are you currently experiencing any systemic symptoms like fever, weight loss, or joint pain?

REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, and Blood Glucose.
REQUEST TEST: Tzanck smear or PCR for Herpes Simplex Virus.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Cellulitis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the details; the description of a central necrotic base with purplish irregular borders and a history of an ant bite, combined with your diabetes and steroid use, makes Ecthyma Gangrenosum or a severe Pyoderma Gangrenosum more likely than typical cellulitis. Given the necrotic features, please avoid starting antibiotics until we confirm the cause. I need to see the wound clearly.

REQUEST IMAGES: High-resolution photograph of the right leg lesion showing the borders and base.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
